formula_checks.name: assetAllocation
formula_checks.why: Only a LINKED account is split by class; a hand-built brokerage that records its own cash sleeve (derive_balance on, cash_balance set) is counted whole under Stocks / Funds, so its cash is shown as stocks. The type says such an account's value IS cash_balance + holdings, so the split is known. Same gap as cashTotal (MK-NW-F-016, batch networth 02); both must use one rule or the Cash class row and the Cash total disagree.
formula_checks.should_be: Linked account → its class breakdown. Hand-built account with a recorded cash sleeve → cash_balance under Cash and the rest under the account's own class. Any other account → whole, under assetClassOf. Invariant: the seven classes sum to total assets, and the Cash class equals cashTotal.
formula_checks.rests_on: AssetAccount type comments on derive_balance and cash_balance; owner DEC-0343 (one concept, one function; totals pinned by invariant).

formula_checks.name: earmarkDefault
formula_checks.why: Every vehicle except the most valuable one, and all valuables, default to 100% earmarked for retirement. A second car losing about 5% a year (the app's own vehicle benchmark) and a jewellery collection then sit inside the 'nest egg' that is projected to fund retirement. They are personal-use property, not retirement savings. (Also unstated: what makes a home 'primary' when re_use is not set.)
formula_checks.should_be: 0% by default for a 529, the primary home, and every account whose class is Personal property (all vehicles and valuables); 100% for everything else, including rental and investment property. A home with no re_use set is asked about, not assumed.
formula_checks.rests_on: The function's own purpose (the share counted towards RETIREMENT); benchmarkReturn's vehicle rate −5%; ordinary planning practice (personal-use assets are not drawn on for retirement income).

formula_checks.name: primaryCarIdOf
formula_checks.why: It picks from accounts whose kind is vehicle OR whose class is Personal property. Personal property also holds valuables, so a $41,000 jewellery collection outranks a $24,300 car and becomes 'the car you drive'; the real car then takes the 100% retirement default. 'Ties to the lowest account id' also leaves text-vs-number order unstated.
formula_checks.should_be: Among accounts whose kind is vehicle only: the largest balance; ties to the lowest id in a stated order. Nothing when there is no vehicle.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own purpose ('the car you drive'); MK-NW-M-006 (Personal property = vehicles and valuables).

formula_checks.name: earmarkedAmount
formula_checks.why: Balance × share, the stated share held to 0–100%, the default only when none is stated. A stated 0% is a stated share and must not fall through to the default — tested in the edge case.

formula_checks.name: retirementEarmarkedValue
formula_checks.why: A straight sum of earmarkedAmount. It inherits the default faults found in MK-NW-F-030 and MK-NW-F-031; its own arithmetic is right. Its cases avoid the disputed defaults so they test the sum.

formula_checks.name: benchmarkReturn
formula_checks.why: The table is internally plausible (equities 10.4%, a mixed brokerage 8%, retirement wrappers 7.9%, cash rates below), and an unknown kind's 6% is labelled a generic estimate by benchmarkInfo. Silent on two cases that change the answer: (1) an override of exactly 0 — 'where they set one' must honour 0 rather than treat it as unset; (2) whether kind ids match ignoring capitals. Note for the owner: options at 5% is not a meaningful expected return for an options position, and the cash rates (checking, savings, money market, CD) move with interest rates and need a dated source — that is benchmarkInfo's job.
formula_checks.should_be: The person's override for the kind whenever one exists, including 0 and negative values; otherwise the table rate; otherwise 6% labelled as a generic estimate. Kind matched exactly as the app's ids are written (state it).
formula_checks.rests_on: Formula in words; ordinary practice (a rate of 0% is a valid setting).

formula_checks.name: benchmarkInfo
formula_checks.why: Source wording and 'edited' follow from benchmarkReturn, but the formula never says how 'estimate' is set, and it inherits the zero-override question (a 0% override must read 'Your custom estimate', edited true).
formula_checks.should_be: edited = an override exists for the kind (0 included); estimate = true for the generic fallback and for any table rate that is an assumption rather than a measured index return — stated per kind.

formula_checks.name: blendedReturn
formula_checks.why: (1) Two formulas describe the nest egg differently: retirementEarmarkedValue (MK-NW-F-033) counts property earmarks (a rental home defaults to 100%), but blendedReturn leaves property out. The rate applied to the pot is then built from a different pot: a $520,000 rental is grown at a rate made only from the 401(k) and savings. (2) '6% when nothing is earmarked' invents a number; with nothing earmarked there is no blended return. It also disagrees with buildAssetsState's 7% fallback (MK-NW-F-039).
formula_checks.should_be: Over exactly the accounts retirementEarmarkedValue counts (property included where earmarked): Σ(earmarked amount × benchmark rate) ÷ Σ earmarked amount. No answer when the earmarked total is zero.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0343 (one concept, one function, over the same set); brief: 'a default number invented where the honest answer is no answer'.

formula_checks.name: buildAssetsState
formula_checks.why: '7% when the total is 0' invents a return for a household that owns nothing, and disagrees with blendedReturn's 6% fallback for the same situation (MK-NW-F-037). The rest is right arithmetic: shares and a balance-weighted average of each account's own target return.
formula_checks.should_be: Total = Σ balances; share = balance ÷ total × 100 (no shares when the total is 0); average target return = Σ(balance × target return) ÷ total, and no answer when the total is 0.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: no invented defaults; consistency with MK-NW-F-037.

formula_checks.name: monthlyContributionsFromOnboarding
formula_checks.why: (1) It adds monthly 'property' contributions (extra mortgage principal, saving for a property) to the contributions that feed the RETIREMENT projection — a rule applied to money it should not touch; that money does not enter the retirement pot. (2) It does not cap contributions at the published limits, so an entry of $2,500/month into a 401(k) projects $30,000 a year where 2026 allows $24,500 for someone under 50. (3) With nothing entered it adds to $0, which reads as 'contributes nothing' rather than 'not answered'. (4) How the employer match is turned into a monthly amount is not stated.
formula_checks.should_be: Monthly retirement contributions = (401(k) capped at the yearly elective limit for the person's age ÷ 12) + (Roth/IRA capped at the IRA limit for the person's age ÷ 12) + investing intended for retirement + the employer match as entered or computed from the stated match rule; property contributions excluded. No answer when onboarding has no contribution answers.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS 2026 limits announced November 2025: 401(k) elective deferral $24,500, IRA $7,500 (with age-50+ catch-ups on top); brief: 'a rule applied to money it should not touch'.

formula_checks.name: sourceWording
formula_checks.why: Matches owner DEC-0301 ('source always, date only when stale') and the 4-or-more-days line is on the right side. Silent on what the words say when the last update is UNKNOWN ('how long ago' of nothing), and on the format of 'how long ago'. The inputs list 'price fetched at' while the words describe the account's last update — which timestamp is used is not stated.
formula_checks.should_be: Linked / Imported, adding ' · updated N days ago' when the last successful update is 4 or more days old, and ' · last update unknown' when there is none on record. State that the timestamp is the account's last successful sync.

formula_checks.name: historyCoverage
formula_checks.why: Years are 'rounded to whole years', so 18 months of history reads '2 years' — the sentence claims more coverage than exists, which is exactly what this function is meant to prevent. The method behind 'months to one decimal' is also not stated.
formula_checks.should_be: Months covered = whole months plus the fraction of the part month (days ÷ days in that month), to one decimal. Sentence: whole years only when the months are an exact multiple of 12; otherwise 'N months' (or 'N years M months'); never rounded up.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own purpose; HistoryCoverage type ('how much of the claimed window is really covered').

formula_checks.name: uberGroupRows
formula_checks.why: Order and totals are right, but the formula never says which classes go to which group. Unclassified ('mixed' — a 401(k) with no holdings listed) and Real estate are the two that matter: the approved drawing puts the home under the third group, and a 401(k) belongs under Investments.
formula_checks.should_be: Cash ← cash. Investments ← stocks_etf, bonds, alternatives, mixed. Property ← real_estate, personal_property. Group total = Σ its classes; groups sum to What you own.
formula_checks.rests_on: Approved drawing 'Net worth, Quiet Instrument v08, state A' (networth 01); owner DEC-0047 (three uber-categories); owner DEC-0072 (cash first).

formula_checks.name: itemizedResultTotal
formula_checks.why: When the remainder is positive and NOT kept as cash, the total falls to the sum of the holdings listed — itemising part of a $186,442 account drops it to $148,001. The screen promises 'We keep the total at $X' (MK-NW-M-038) and the author rule says itemising never changes what an account is worth. When the holdings come to MORE than the entered total, raising the total silently is also a change of value the person never confirmed.
formula_checks.should_be: Remainder ≥ 0: total stays the entered total (the remainder is kept, either as cash or as an 'not itemised' line). Remainder < 0: no new total until the person confirms the higher figure.
formula_checks.rests_on: Figure MK-NW-M-038 words ('We keep the total at $X'); author rule on M-038.

formula_checks.name: buildItemizedAccounts
formula_checks.why: (1) A bond gets face value = its current value — an invented number; face and value differ, and theBonds shows them side by side precisely because they differ, so every yield to maturity on an itemised bond comes out wrong. (2) The new accounts copy institution and tax bucket but not the original's retirement earmark (or kind), so a lump earmarked 40% for retirement becomes accounts at the 100% default and the nest egg jumps from itemising alone. (3) A remainder not kept as cash is dropped (see MK-NW-F-051).
formula_checks.should_be: Each new account also copies the original's kind/wrapper, retirement share and source; a bond's face value is left unknown (asked for) unless the person enters it; a remainder not kept as cash is kept as a 'not itemised' account so the balances still sum to the entered total.
formula_checks.rests_on: Author rule on MK-NW-M-053 (face and value shown side by side because they differ); author rule on M-038; brief: 'a default number invented'.
